status: PASS for saved actual-native warm plain Chat text/tool-heavy measurements and all four memory controls. This is not cold-heap, aggregate-capacity or full original-protocol native acceptance. Current source has an explicit five-path test/sink-child metadata reuse bridge; the saved runs are not described as freshly measured at every committed byte.

measuredToCommittedBridge.reason: Added the lint-required describe wrapper; corpus, runner and assertions are unchanged.
Type-only body return annotations include the existing parsed chunks scalar; runtime schema already included chunks during measurement.
Keep chunks out of shared public request records; pass the same scalar at unchanged sample points to the sink-child callback. Hashing and byte handling are unchanged.
Added small isolated-HTTP parity and route-loss assertions; this file does not execute in the measured probe.
Move the chunks scalar from the request object to callback-local IPC metadata in the unmeasured sink child; no body buffering or sampling-protocol change.

rootCause.falseNativeProof: The old wrapper dropped the optional native capability; an environment-derived native flag did not prove provider route selection. Commit 7357d2c3c forwards the original capability object.
rootCause.followup: Forward actual count, pending metadata and receiver/signal-bound operations on the typed snapshot. The handle borrows the fixture-owned pin. Require scalar observations of native body/estimate and zero legacy spool/estimator-file operations.
rootCause.harnessFix: Do not add chunks to shared sink request records: unchanged strict equality expects bytes/hash/contentLength only. The isolated child reports chunks through callback-local IPC metadata.
rootCause.setup: The native corpus writer emits the same original rows incrementally, and native fixture setup commits one row at a time. The previous shared seeder batches at 256 rows, not a whole-history array. No claim that that seeder caused a production leak is made.
rootCause.production: No production source changed after the capability checkpoint. No production leak was demonstrated or fixed by this warm-only evidence.

protocol.name: separate-native-warm-plain-chat-1pair-6retention
protocol.nativeWarmup: One separately costed actual prepare/estimate/HTTP send of each size, equally for text and tools.
protocol.unchanged: Thresholds, Theil-Sen retained predicate, settledHeap, GC settings, engine settings, quiet-baseline schedule and 180000 ms file timeout.
protocol.noSpecial5MiBThreshold: The actual sendPeak contract has a 1 MiB large-minus-small growth and retained-trend allowance. Its eager traps hold original row arrays and do not use a separate fixed 5 MiB threshold.
protocol.peakMeaning: peakHeap and peakArrayBuffers are increases over each send baseline; peakRss is provider-probe resident bytes. Absolute retained readings remain in each series.

owningProcesses.oracle: Parent setup process computes independent old-converter bodies outside child measurement; only hashes/counts cross to the result. No expected 8 MiB body is retained in the measured provider probe.
owningProcesses.provider: Bun probe owns native HistoryService, pinned sources, provider, runtime tokenizer and memory sampling.
owningProcesses.sink: Separate HTTP child incrementally hashes network chunks; it owns socket buffers, hash state and scalar request metadata, not a complete buffered body. Sink memory/CPU is not included in provider readings.

protocol.observerState: Only scalar native-route counts and the existing capped 64 WeakRefs; no row map or body copy.
protocol.costUnits: elapsedMs and process.cpuUsage microseconds belong to the provider probe including setup/sampling; journalBytesAdded is exact net journal subtree size growth, not cumulative write bytes. Darwin fsRead/fsWrite are uninterpreted kernel counters.
limitations: One measured pair is not the original three-pair native protocol.
Warm zero net journal growth is not a physical-read or no-I/O proof.
One live pin per size and six sends do not establish aggregate cache/pin/overlay capacity.
